correctness.rationale: PASS: The exact product binom(q p^a,p^a)=q prod_{1<=j<p^a}(1+(q-1)p^a/j) is p-integral. Every factor has slope divisible by p, giving H(q+p^kt)-H(q)=p^kt mod p^(k+1), while (q+p^kt)^(p^a)-q^(p^a)=0 mod p^(k+1), also for p=2 and k=1. Fermat starts all p classes at level1, and one digit of Hensel lifting is forced at every level. Therefore exactly p classes modulo p^a (one zero and p-1 units); fixed-modulus Dirichlet PNT yields (p-1)/phi(p^a)=1/p^(a-1) relative density among primes. Independently enumerated exact original binomial residues for small p,a and saw unique lifts; finite checks only corroborate unrestricted p-adic argument.

evidence: Full prior tower theorem states p>=5 and fixed q and classifies initial exponent segment through v_p(beta_pq-omega_p(q)).
broader_coverage.reasoning: The closest prior applies to p>=5, q prime, a variable, and characterizes a fixed q tower. It does not prove the p-adic simple-root condition as q varies, nor identify p-1 reduced classes at each p^a, and excludes p=2,3. The 2026 motivating arXiv square criterion is narrower in exponent.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The fixed-q tower theorem plus prime-number theorem in progressions alone cannot imply one root per residue at each p^a. It needs the base-variable unit-slope congruence, reconstructed directly from the integral product. The resulting prime density follows after that new classification.

evidence: The local slope F(q+p^kt)-F(q)=p^kt modulo p^(k+1) gives one root above each q mod p; tower theorem uses beta_pq versus omega_p(q) to bound a for a fixed base.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The same binomial congruence can be expressed as p-adic zeros of F_{p^a}(q)=binom(qp^a,p^a)-q^(p^a), or as an exact simple-root Hensel lift of the identity q-q^p modulo p. The earlier tower theorem instead fixes q and varies a; these quantifiers cannot be interchanged.

value.rationale: PASS: Characterizing precisely which prime bases solve a natural binomial congruence at every fixed prime power, with one class above each mod-p unit and an exact prime density, is a useful global arithmetic classification rather than an isolated modular check. Uniform-in-a lifting and small-prime inclusions extend the parameter directions of published tower criteria. Generic Hensel lemma and Dirichlet PNT are credited, not claimed as new.

limitations: No explicit closed-form formulas for each lifted nontrivial root or uniform PNT error as p,a vary; p-adic proof is infinite, enumeration finite.
